title: Research Note: The Sixty-One Activity Pairs of Jeevan

passages.text: Scope: This note sets out all sixty-one activity pairs of jeevan as the primary texts give them, pair by pair, with the bal and shakti member of each named from the tabulated enumeration and defined from the detailed definitions. It records what the two sources agree on, where the definitional language cuts against the tabulated assignment, and which variants or pair-relations the texts leave unsettled.

The inventory is documentary. It does not propose a functional interpretation of the pairs; that interpretation is in the technical companion, and the questions this inventory leaves open are collected in §8.

passages.heading: 1-why-the-inventory-exists
passages.text: 1. Why the inventory exists

passages.heading: 1-why-the-inventory-exists
passages.text: The 122 activities are the finest-grained account the sources give of what jeevan does. They are stated twice: once as a table that assigns every activity to a column, and once as definitions that describe each activity in a sentence or two. Both are needed, and neither is sufficient alone.

passages.heading: 1-why-the-inventory-exists
passages.text: The table fixes which member of a pair is the bal and which the shakti. The definitions fix what each activity is about. The two are consistent in their ordering throughout, but the definitions cannot be used to recover the assignment, because in several places the language of a definition points the opposite way from the column it sits in (§6). A reading that classified the activities by what their definitions sound like would therefore disagree with the sources at identifiable points. Setting both out together is the only way to keep the assignment source-governed.

passages.heading: 2-the-two-source-presentations
passages.text: 2. The two source presentations

passages.heading: 2-the-two-source-presentations
passages.text: The tabulated enumeration appears as Table 1, “122 conducts of awakened jeevan”, with the decomposition 2×(1+2+8+18+32)=2×61=122 printed as its subtitle (AVD, pp. 91–94). It has five columns:

passages.heading: 2-the-two-source-presentations
passages.text: Column Hindi Content 1 akshay bal ki kriyayen (pratyavartan) The activities of inexhaustible bal, under reflection 2 akshay bal ka naam The name of the inexhaustible bal — the faculty 3 jeevan ka avayav The constituent of jeevan — nucleus or orbit 4 akshay shakti ka naam The name of the inexhaustible shakti — the orientation 5 akshay shakti ki kriyayen (paravartan) The activities of inexhaustible shakti, under projection

passages.heading: 2-the-two-source-presentations
passages.text: The middle three columns carry the faculty-level naming and the outer two the activity-level partition, which is why one table states both grains at which strength and power are used. The English rendering in the source translates bal and shakti inconsistently, using “power” for both in the column heads and “force” for shakti in its name column; the Hindi बल and शक्ति is unambiguous and is what this inventory follows.

passages.heading: 2-the-two-source-presentations
passages.text: The detailed definitions run under the heading “The Definitions of 122 activities of Jeevan” (MVD, pp. 328–348). Each faculty’s block opens with its two modes, and the activities beneath are set out as two-name headings followed by a definition of each member. The block headings are realisation and authenticity for atma, enlightenment and resolve for buddhi, contemplation and visualisation for chitta, deliberation and analysis for vritti, and selection and taste for mun (MVD, pp. 328, 329, 332, 339).

passages.heading: 3-the-five-loci
passages.text: 3. The five loci

passages.heading: 3-the-five-loci
passages.text: Constituent Faculty (bal) Orientation (shakti) Bal activity Shakti activity Pairs Activities Nucleus Atma Praman, evidence Anubhav, realisation Pramanikta, authenticity 1 2 First orbit Buddhi Ritambhara, resoluteness Bodh, enlightenment Sankalp, resolve 2 4 Second orbit Chitta Ichha, desire Chintan, contemplation Chitran, visualisation 8 16 Third orbit Vritti Vichar, thought Tulan, deliberation Vishleshan, analysis 18 36 Fourth orbit Mun Asha, hope Asvadan, taste Chayan, selection 32 64 61 122

passages.heading: 3-the-five-loci
passages.text: Every pair below occupies one position at one of these loci. The numbering within each faculty is the source’s own (AVD, pp. 91–94). The numbered rows are contents of the generic pair named in this table, not a second set of faculties and not dimensions of it. The sources use “eight dimensions” for visualisation in chitta, and they do not map those dimensions onto the eight chitta pairs (§4.3). For mun, asha names the orientation—hope toward tasting—while asvadan and chayan are the two activities; the thirty-two pairs are what that tasting and selecting are over.

passages.heading: 4-the-sixty-one-pairs
passages.text: 4. The sixty-one pairs

passages.heading: 4-the-sixty-one-pairs
passages.text: The Hindi activity names and their bal–shakti column assignments follow the AVD table. English glosses follow AVD where its rendering is stable and MVD where the detailed definition supplies the clearer term; §8 records material differences. The two definition columns condense MVD, retaining only the governing clauses where a definition runs longer. Each cell gives that clause first in Hindi as printed, then in the published English, so the translation can be checked against the source wording rather than inferred from the English alone. Temperature and the six tastes require two parallel documentary views because the AVD assignments and MVD definition headings do not divide the content in the same way (§4.5).

passages.heading: 4-the-sixty-one-pairs
passages.text: 4.1 Atma — one pair

passages.heading: 4-the-sixty-one-pairs
passages.text: # Bal entry Condensed MVD definition Shakti entry Condensed MVD definition 1 anubhav — realisation, in astitva सत्ता में संपृक्त प्रकृति के रूप में नित्य वर्तमान।Eternal presence in the form of nature saturated in Omnipotence pramanikta — authenticity, of paramanand अनुभव संपन्न अभिव्यक्ति, संप्रेषणा, प्रकाशन।Realisation-based expression, communication and exposition

passages.heading: 4-the-sixty-one-pairs
passages.text: Atma’s pair is named twice over. The tabulated enumeration gives the modes, realisation and authenticity; the definitions give their contents, existence and ultimate bliss, under the sub-heading “Realisation in existence / Authenticity of ultimate bliss” (MVD, p. 328).

passages.heading: 4-the-sixty-one-pairs
passages.text: 4.2 Buddhi — two pairs

passages.heading: 4-the-sixty-one-pairs
passages.text: # Bal entry Condensed MVD definition Shakti entry Condensed MVD definition 1 anand — bliss अंतविहीन (बिना रूकावट) उत्सव क्रिया।Endless, uninterrupted celebration activity dhee उत्सवशीलता का प्रवर्तन क्रिया (परावर्तन के लिए तत्परता)।The inclination activity of celebration, readiness for projection 2 astitva — existence स्थिति, गति, विकास, जागृति और वर्तमान सहज निर्भ्रम स्वीकृति।Acceptance free from delusion of state, motion, development, awakening, and the present dhruti सहअस्तित्व सहज सत्य में निष्ठा और परावर्तित करने के लिए प्रवृति; भय का अभाव, वर्तमान में विश्वास।Dedication in truth as coexistence and tendency for projection; absence of fear, trust in the present

passages.heading: 4-the-sixty-one-pairs
passages.text: Buddhi’s block carries the one sentence in the whole enumeration that names the partition of a pair outright: the pinnacle of acceptance of the state and motion of awakening is bliss and dhee (MVD, p. 328). Both of its pairs place an acceptance against a readiness for projection.

passages.heading: 4-the-sixty-one-pairs
passages.text: 4.3 Chitta — eight pairs

passages.heading: 4-the-sixty-one-pairs
passages.text: # Bal entry Condensed MVD definition Shakti entry Condensed MVD definition 1 shruti — revelation यथार्थ समझदारी का भाषाकरण; यथार्थ जीवन व दर्शन पूर्ण अभिव्यक्ति।Articulation of understanding of reality; the expression of knowledge of jeevan and holistic view of existence smriti — memory बार-बार आवश्यकतानुसार भाषा पूर्वक समझ का प्रस्तुतीकरण।Presentation of understanding through language as many times as necessary 2 medha — intellect स्मृति का धारक-वाहक क्रिया।The carrier-bearer activity of memory kala — art उपयोगिता योग्य सुंदर क्रिया।Beautification activity along with usefulness 3 kanti — radiance सार्थकता संभावना के अर्थ में स्पष्ट होना प्रकाश है।Light as the clarity of meaning as possibility roop — form आकार, आयतन, धन।Shape, volume, and density 4 nireekshan — inspection अनुभव मूलक दर्शन व उसके प्रकटन की संयुक्त चिंतन चित्रण क्रिया।Realisation-based holistic view, manifesting as contemplation combined with visualisation guna — properties सापेक्ष गतियाँ; सम-विषम-मध्यस्थ गतियाँ, गतियों का आंकलन।Relative motions; assessment of generative, degenerative, and mediative motion 5 santosh — contentment अभाव का अभाव।The lack of the sentiment of lacking shree — abundance समृद्धि या समृद्धि की निरंतरता सहज स्वीकृति।Prosperity, or acceptance of continuity of prosperity 6 prem — love पूर्णानुभूति; पूर्णता में रति व उसकी निरंतरता।Realisation of the complete; devotion in completeness and its continuity ananyata — non-otherness मानव की परस्परता व नैसर्गिकता में पूरक क्रिया-कलाप।Complementary activity in mutuality of humans and with the rest of nature 7 vatsalya — guidance अभ्युदय के अर्थ में पोषण, संरक्षण की निरंतरता।The continuity of nurturing and protection for comprehensive resolution sahajta — effortlessness स्पष्टता व प्रामाणिकता; व्यवहार, रीति, विचार एवं अनुभव की एकसूत्रता।Clarity and authenticity; integrality of behaviour, norm, thought and realisation 8 shraddha — reverence श्रेय की ओर गतिशीलता अर्थात् आचरण पूर्णता की ओर गुणात्मक परिवर्तन।Movement towards righteousness, qualitative transformation towards conduct completeness pujyata — devoutness गुणात्मक विकास और जागृति के लिए सक्रियता।Activeness for qualitative development and awakening

passages.heading: 4-the-sixty-one-pairs
passages.text: Visualisation in chitta is separately described through eight dimensions: form, property, count, time, expanse, effort, motion, and result (MVD, p. 327). The source does not map those dimensions one-to-one onto the eight bal–shakti pairs in this block.

passages.heading: 4-the-sixty-one-pairs
passages.text: 4.4 Vritti — eighteen pairs

passages.heading: 4-the-sixty-one-pairs
passages.text: # Bal entry Condensed MVD definition Shakti entry Condensed MVD definition 1 vidya — learning जो जैसा है, अर्थात् जिस प्रयोजनार्थ है उसे वैसा ही विधिवत् जानने, मानने, स्वीकार करने की क्रिया।Systematically knowing, believing and accepting something as it is, i.e. the purpose of its being pragya — intelligence परिष्कृति पूर्ण संचेतना; वस्तुगत सत्य, वस्तु स्थिति सत्य के प्रति अवधारणा।Completely refined human consciousness; manifestation of conception of objective and relative truth 2 keerti — repute जागृति की ओर सक्रियता।The activeness for awakening vichar — thought स्फुरण पूर्वक सत्यता को उद्घाटित करने हेतु की गई क्रिया; सहअस्तित्व सहज प्रकाशन, संप्रेषणा।Unfolding of verity with exuberance; the exposition and communication of coexistence 3 nishchaya — certitude सत्यतापूर्ण विचार की निरंतरता।Continuity of thought of verity dhairya — patience न्यायपूर्ण विचार की निरंतरता।Continuity of just thoughts 4 shanti — peace समाधान पूर्ण विचार का फलन; इच्छा एवं विचार की निर्विरोधिता।Consequence of resolved thoughts; absence of resistance in desire and thought daya — kindness दूसरे के विकास में हस्तक्षेप न करना; पात्रता के अनुरूप वस्तु, योग्यता प्रदायी क्षमता।Not interfering in others’ awakening; instilling content and ability according to their receptivity 5 krupa — grace दूसरे के विकास के लिए सहायता अथवा पात्रता अर्जित करने में सहायक होने में अर्हता सम्पन्न रहना।Being capable of helping another’s awakening or acquiring of receptivity karuna — compassion विकास के लिए उत्प्रेरित करना; योग्यता और पात्रता अर्जित करने में सहायक होना।Inspiring others for awakening; being helpful to their acquiring ability and receptivity 6 dum — uprightness ह्रास की ओर जो आसक्ति है, उसकी समापन क्रिया; भ्रम, भय और अपव्ययता से मुक्ति।The act of ending attachment towards decline; liberation from delusion, fear and wastefulness kshama — forgiveness विकास के लिए की जाने वाली सहायता के समय उसके ह्रास पक्ष से अप्रभावित रहना।Remaining unaffected from another’s aspect of decline while helping them for awakening 7 tatparta — readiness जागृति क्रम में सक्रियता; उत्पादन में लगनशीलता; मानवीय व्यवहार-आचरण में निष्ठा।Activeness in awakening; perseverance in production; dedication in humane behaviour utsah — enthusiasm उत्थान के लिए साहस; व्यवस्था सहज सजगता।Intrepidity for rising; awareness of the orderliness 8 kritagyata — gratitude जिस किसी की भी सहायता से उन्नति की प्राप्ति में सहायता मिली हो, उसकी स्वीकृति।The acceptance of help received from anyone for advancement saumyata — humility स्वेच्छा से स्वयं का नियंत्रण; स्वभावगति प्रतिष्ठा अर्थात् शिष्टता।Wilful self-restraint; being established in the natural state, i.e. civility 9 gaurav — glory निर्विरोध पूर्वक अंगीकार किये गये अनुकरण।Embracing to emulate without resistance saralta — simplicity ग्रन्थि व तनाव रहित अगंहार।Demeanour devoid of complexity and tension 10 vishwas — trust परस्परता में निहित मूल्य निर्वाह।Fulfilment of values inherent in mutuality saujanyata — concordance सहकारिता, सहभागिता, सहयोगिता, पूरकता।Collaboration, co-participation, cooperation, complementariness 11 satya — truth जो तीनों काल में एक सा भासमान, विद्यमान एवं अनुभव गम्य है।That which is uniformly perceivable, existent and realisable at all times dharma धारणा ही धर्म है; जिससे जिसका विलगीकरण न हो।Innateness itself; that from which its separation does not happen 12 nyaya — justice संबंधों व मूल्यों की पहचान व निर्वाह तथा मूल्यांकन व उभयतृप्ति क्रिया।Recognition of relationships, fulfilling of values, evaluation, and mutual satisfaction samvedna — sensitivity पूर्णता के अर्थ में वेगित होना; सभी ज्ञानेन्द्रियों द्वारा बाह्य संकेतों को ग्रहण करना; व्यवस्था के प्रति तत्परता।Movement for completeness; grasping external sensory indications through all cognitive organs; readiness for participation in the orderliness 13 tadatmayata — absolute-oneness नित्यता के अर्थ में स्वीकार सहित किया गया निर्णय।The decision made along with acceptance towards eternalness sahas — intrepidity सहनशीलता समेत प्रसन्नता सहित किया गया व्यवहार क्रिया कलाप।Work and behaviour performed with happiness along with endurance 14 samyama — restraint मानवीयता पूर्ण विचार, व्यवहार एवम् व्यवसाय में नियंत्रित होना।Being regulated in humane thought, behaviour and vocation niyam — law नियंत्रण पूर्ण स्वयंस्फूर्त विधि से समग्र व्यवस्था में भागीदारी करने की प्रवृत्ति और प्रमाण।The tendency and evidence of participating in the overall orderliness while self-regulated 15 veerta — courage अन्य को न्याय दिलाने में स्व-शक्तियों का नियोजन।Utilising one’s powers to ensure delivery of justice to others dheerta — fortitude न्याय के प्रति निष्ठा एवं दृढ़ता।Dedication and firmness towards justice 16 bhav — sentiment, value मौलिकता = मूल्य = जिम्मेदारी, भागीदारी।Essentiality, value, responsibility, participation samveg — impetus संयोग से प्राप्त गति।The momentum acquired from meaningful union 17 jati — kind रूप, गुण, स्वभाव व धर्म की विशिष्टता।The uniqueness of form, properties, essential nature and dharma kaal — time क्रिया की अवधि।Duration of activity 18 tushti — satiation समझदारी पूर्वक छ: सद्गुणों से संपन्न होना, परिवार में समाधान-समृद्धि; अखंड समाज में भागीदारी।Accomplishment of the six merits, resolution and prosperity in the family, participation in the undivided society pushti — confirmation तुष्टि का निरंतर मूल्यांकन; मानव परंपरा के रूप में उसका लोकव्यापीकरण।Continuous evaluation of satiation; its dissemination in the form of human tradition

passages.heading: 4-the-sixty-one-pairs
passages.text: 4.5 Mun — thirty-two pairs

passages.heading: 4-the-sixty-one-pairs
passages.text: The left-hand column belongs to asvadan; the right-hand column to chayan. A row places both members at one position in mun. It does not state that the shakti member is the selection of that taste. The first twenty-two are relational and dispositional; the last ten are the activities of the cognitive and work organs, set out under their own sub-heading (MVD, p. 347).

passages.heading: 4-the-sixty-one-pairs
passages.text: # Bal entry Condensed MVD definition Shakti entry Condensed MVD definition 1 bhakti — devotion भय से मुक्त होने का क्रियाकलाप और भ्रम मुक्ति; भक्ति संपूर्ण निष्ठा की अभिव्यक्ति है।Becoming liberated from fear and delusion; total dedication tanmayata — immersion जागृति सहज प्रभाव में अभिभूत होना, निश्चित लक्ष्य एवं दिशा हेतु।Being enthralled in the effect of awakening, with definite goal and direction 2 mamta — care अपनत्व की पराकाष्ठा पूर्वक पोषण संरक्षण; स्वयं की प्रतिरूपता की स्वीकृति।Nurturing and protecting with the pinnacle of affinity; accepting the other as an image of oneself udarta — generosity दूसरों की जीवन जागृति, शरीर स्वस्थता व समृद्धि के लिए तन, मन, धन का अर्पण-समर्पण।Offering body, mind and wealth as needed for another’s awakening, health and prosperity 3 samman — respect व्यक्तित्व, प्रतिभा की स्वीकृति।The acceptance of personality and talent sauhardta — cordiality अवधारणा, अनुभव, स्मृति और श्रुति को यथावत् प्रस्तुत करने का क्रियाकलाप।Presenting conception, realisation, memory, and shruti (realised articulation) as accepted 4 sneha — affection न्यायपूर्ण व्यवहार में निर्विरोधिता।Absence of resistance in just behaviour nishtha — dedication जागृति पूर्ण लक्ष्य को प्राप्त करने व प्रमाणित करने का निरंतर प्रयास।Continuous endeavour of attaining and evidencing the goal of complete awakening 5 putra-putri — son, daughter शरीर रचना की कारकता सहज स्वीकृति और जीवन जागृति में पूरकता निर्वाह करने वाली मानव इकाई ही पिता है।Acceptance of parents as having given birth and being complementary for awakening anurag — devotedness निर्भ्रमता में प्राप्त आप्लावन; संबंधों में निहित मूल्यों का निर्वाह करने में सफलता।Immersion obtained in absence of delusion; success in fulfilling the values inherent in relationships 6 swami, sathi — master सर्वतोमुखी समाधान प्राप्त व्यक्ति; स्वयं को जानकर निर्वाह करने के क्रम में साथी।One who has attained comprehensive resolution and fulfils relationships upon knowing the self dayitva — responsibility व्यवहार, व्यवसाय एवं व्यवस्थात्मक संबंधों में मूल्यानुभूति सहित शिष्टतापूर्ण व्यवहार।Civilised behaviour with realisation of values in behaviour, vocation and orderliness 7 sevak, sahyogi — associate अभ्युदय के अर्थ में मार्गदर्शक के साथ-साथ अनुगमन करना; उत्पादन में सहयोगी होना।One who moves with acceptance behind the guide for comprehensive resolution; helpful in production kartavya — duty प्रत्येक स्तर में प्राप्त संबंधों एवं सम्पर्कों में निहित मूल्यों का निर्वाह।Fulfilling values inherent in relationships and associations at every level 8 svayatta — self-reliance समृद्धि का अनुभव ही स्वायत्त है।The realisation of prosperity samriddhi — prosperity आवश्यकता से अधिक उत्पादन समृद्धि है।Production more than needs 9 hita — health शरीर सीमान्तवर्तीय उपयोगिता।Usefulness within purview of the body svasthya — wellness मन एवं प्रवृत्तियों के अनुसार कर्मेन्द्रिय व ज्ञानेन्द्रियों का कार्य करने योग्य स्थिति।Cognitive and work organs able to work according to mun and the tendencies 10 priya — pleasant ज्ञानेन्द्रियों के लिए शरीर स्वस्थता के अर्थ में अनुकूल योग संयोग।Conduciveness of the five sensory organs with respect to bodily wellness pravrittiyan — tendencies परावर्तन हेतु जीवन में होने वाली आशा, विचार, इच्छा, संकल्प एवं प्रामाणिकता।Hope, thought, desire, resolve and authenticity taking place in jeevan for projection 11 ullas — elation मुखरण; उत्थान की ओर पारदर्शक प्रस्तुति।Articulation; transparent presentation haas — merriness समाधान सहित प्रसन्नता व मुस्कान सहित मानवीय लक्ष्य व दिशा की ओर गति।Movement towards humane goal and direction with resolution and joyousness 12 sheel — modesty जागृति सहज वैभव को शिष्टता के रूप में प्रामाणिकता को इंगित कर लेना।Identifying the grandeur of awakening in all dimensions with authenticity as civility sankoch — politeness अस्वीकृति को शिष्टता से प्रस्तुत करना।Expressing disagreement in a civilised way 13 guru शिक्षा-संस्कार से जिज्ञासाओं को समाधान के रूप में अवधारणा में प्रस्थापित करने वाला मानव।One who imparts conception as resolution of inquiries through education-sanskar pramanik — authentic प्रमाणों का धारक वाहक; प्रयोग, व्यवहार, अनुभवपूर्ण विधि से प्रमाणों के रूप में जीना।Bearer and carrier of evidence; living as evidence through experiment, behaviour, and realisation 14 shishya — disciple शिक्षा-संस्कार ग्रहण-स्वीकार के लिए प्रस्तुत व्यक्ति, जिसमें गुरु का सम्बन्ध स्वीकृत हो।One ready to accept education-sanskar, in whom the relationship of guru is accepted jigyasu — inquirer निर्भ्रम शिक्षा ग्रहण करने के लिए तीव्र इच्छा का प्रकाशन।Demonstration of strong desire for delusion-free education 15 bhai-mitra — brother, friend एकोदर को भाई का संबोधन; भाईवत् स्वीकृतियाँ या मित्र।One born of the same womb; brother-like acceptance pragati — progress समग्र व्यवस्था में भागीदारी; समाधान प्रधान अपेक्षा, प्रक्रिया और प्रमाण।Participation in the overall orderliness, with emphasis on resolution 16 bahan — sister एकोदरीय अथवा एकोदरवत् बहनें।One born of the same womb; sister-like acceptance unnati — advancement समृद्धि प्रधान अपेक्षा, प्रक्रिया व प्रमाण; जागृति की ओर गति।Expectation, process and evidence of prosperity; movement towards awakening 17 sweekruti — acceptance अनुभव मूलक प्रभाव में इंगित संकेतों को यथावत् परावर्तन में प्रमाणित करने की क्रिया।Evidencing in projection what has been received owing to realisation-based effect swagat — reception नियम, न्याय, समाधान, सत्य सहज स्वीकृतियों के लिए तैयारियाँ।The preparations for evidencing the acceptances of law, justice, resolution, truth 18 ruchi — interest अनुकूल भौतिक-रासायनिक वस्तुओं के योग-संयोग से प्राप्त परिणामों की पहचान।Recognition of results from the contact of conducive physicochemical things with the senses pehchan — recognition इन्द्रिय सन्निकर्ष में आवश्यक तत्व; योग-संयोग से प्राप्त कुल परिणाम की स्वीकृति।Identification of necessary elements in sensory contact; acceptance of the result of yog-sanyog 19 sukh — happiness समाधान।Resolution sfoorti — motivation समाधान सहज प्रमाणों में, से, के लिए प्रवृत्ति।The tendency in, by, for evidence of resolution 20 pati, patni — husband, wife पति-पत्नी।The spousal relationship yatitva, satitva — diligence, steadfastness यत्न पूर्वक तथा सत्व (संकल्प) पूर्वक तरने-जागृति के लिए किया गया कार्य-व्यवहार।Work and behaviour performed effortfully, and truthfully with resolve, for emancipation and awakening 21 mata — mother शरीर रचना की कारकता सहज स्वीकृति और जीवन जागृति में पूरकता निर्वाह।Acceptance of having given birth and being complementary for awakening poshan — nurturing इकाई + अनुकूल इकाई।Unit plus conducive unit 22 pita — father पोषण, सुरक्षा की स्वीकृति।Acceptance of providing nurturing and protection sanrakshan — protection निर्बाधता; सुगमता के अर्थ में।Removing obstacles, for ease

passages.heading: 4-the-sixty-one-pairs
passages.text: The sensory block opens with touch, named on both sides in both presentations.

passages.heading: 4-the-sixty-one-pairs
passages.text: # Bal entry Condensed MVD definition Shakti entry Condensed MVD definition 23 mridu, kathor — soft, hard स्पर्शेंद्रिय से कम या अधिक भार व दबाव को सहने वाली वस्तुएँ।What bears less or more weight or pressure than touch vahan, samvahan — bearability संवहन-मृदु: संकुचन पूर्वक वहन करने वाली वस्तुएँ।A shared bearing passage; the two terms are not defined separately

passages.heading: 4-the-sixty-one-pairs
passages.text: Temperature and the six tastes require two parallel records. AVD assigns each sensory entry to the bal column and repeats poshan in the shakti column. This preserves seven of the thirty-two tabulated pair positions.

passages.heading: 4-the-sixty-one-pairs
passages.text: # AVD bal assignment AVD shakti assignment 24 sheet, ushna — cold, hot poshan — nourishing 25 khatta — sour poshan — nourishing 26 meetha — sweet poshan — nourishing 27 chirchira — pungent poshan — nourishing 28 kadua — bitter poshan — nourishing 29 kasaila — astringent poshan — nourishing 30 khara — salty poshan — nourishing

passages.heading: 4-the-sixty-one-pairs
passages.text: MVD instead heads each position by the sensory quality and defines it through the shared contrast poshan / shoshan — nourishing / depleting — without separately defining a second member at each position (pp. 347–348).

passages.heading: 4-the-sixty-one-pairs
passages.text: # MVD sensory heading MVD defining contrast 24 sheet, ushna — cold, hot पोषण/शोषण।Nurturing or depriving contact 25 khatta — sour पोषण/शोषण।Taste recognised on contact of the tongue 26 meetha — sweet पोषण/शोषण।Taste recognised on contact of the tongue 27 charpara — pungent पोषण/शोषण।Taste recognised on contact of the tongue 28 kadua — bitter पोषण/शोषण।Taste recognised on contact of the tongue 29 kasaila — astringent पोषण/शोषण।Taste recognised on contact of the tongue 30 khara — salty पोषण/शोषण।Taste recognised on contact of the tongue

passages.heading: 4-the-sixty-one-pairs
passages.text: MVD defines the shared contrast as: poshan, इकाई + अनुकूल इकाई; shoshan, इकाई − अनुकूल इकाई अथवा इकाई + प्रतिकूल इकाई — unit plus a conducive unit, against a unit lacking a conducive unit or joined with an unconducive unit (p. 348). AVD therefore establishes seven repeated shakti assignments, while MVD supplies one recurring criterion or correlate. The sources do not settle whether the seven repetitions denote seven distinct activities, one recurrent activity applied to seven sensory fields, or tabular shorthand. The inventory retains both views rather than converting either into the other.

passages.heading: 4-the-sixty-one-pairs
passages.text: Smell and visible form are again two-name pairs.

passages.heading: 4-the-sixty-one-pairs
passages.text: # Bal entry Condensed MVD definition Shakti entry Condensed MVD definition 31 sugandh, durgandh — pleasant, unpleasant smell सुगन्ध/दुर्गन्ध।What is received through smell shvasan, nihshvasan — inhalation, exhalation प्रश्वसन/विश्वसन।Respiratory movement associated with smell 32 suroop, kuroop — beautiful, ugly सुरूप/कुरूप।What is received through visible form swagat, aswagat — affinity, otherness अपनापन/परायापन।Affinity or otherness in response to visible form

passages.heading: 4-the-sixty-one-pairs
passages.text: The purpose of the sensory group is stated with it: every awakened human recognises that the purpose of sensations is maintaining the health of the body (MVD, pp. 347–348). In delusion, taste and selection already operate over this sensory and instinctual field; the thirty-two pairs as defined are the awakened inventory of mun’s two generic activities, not a further set that remains unused from lack of need (the architecture note §4.2, §6).

passages.heading: 5-what-the-two-presentations-agree-on
passages.section: 5. What the two presentations agree on
passages.text: 5. What the two presentations agree on

passages.heading: 5-what-the-two-presentations-agree-on
passages.section: 5. What the two presentations agree on
passages.text: The left–right order is the same where both presentations supply two names. Each detailed heading places the member corresponding to the bal column first and the member corresponding to the shakti column second. The agreement extends to compound entries, where mridu-kathor stands against vahan-samvahan in the definitions exactly as the columns place them (MVD, p. 347; AVD, p. 93). Temperature and the six tastes are the exception: AVD supplies two columns and repeats poshan, whereas MVD heads each sensory quality and defines it through poshan/shoshan without a separately defined second member (§4.5, §8). Three closing entries also differ in their actual names, so their agreement is positional rather than lexical (§8).

passages.heading: 5-what-the-two-presentations-agree-on
passages.section: 5. What the two presentations agree on
passages.text: That agreement is worth stating because the two presentations are otherwise independent: one is a table of names with no definitions, the other a run of definitions with no columns. Their concurrence on ordering is what allows either to be read against the other, and it means the bal member of any pair can be identified from the definitions alone by position, though not by content (§6).

passages.heading: 5-what-the-two-presentations-agree-on
passages.section: 5. What the two presentations agree on
passages.text: Naming differs in places without affecting the assignment. Shruti is rendered “revelation” in the table and “realised articulation” in the definitions; pushti is “validation” against “confirmation”; jati is “species” against “kind”; bhav is “value” against “sentiment”; ananyata is “non-dualness” against “non-otherness”. These are translation variants of one Hindi term in each case.

passages.heading: 6-where-the-definitions-cut-against-the-column
passages.section: 6. Where the definitions cut against the column
passages.text: 6. Where the definitions cut against the column

passages.heading: 6-where-the-definitions-cut-against-the-column
passages.section: 6. Where the definitions cut against the column
passages.text: The tabulated assignment cannot be recovered from the definitions by reading which of the two sounds more like a state and which more like a motion. In the following pairs that procedure gives the wrong answer or no answer, which is why the table governs.

passages.heading: 6-where-the-definitions-cut-against-the-column
passages.section: 6. Where the definitions cut against the column
passages.text: Pair Tabulated assignment What the definition says Why the reading misleads veerta / dheerta veerta is the bal Veerta is “utilising one’s powers to ensure delivery of justice to others”; dheerta is “dedication and firmness towards justice” The bal member is defined by outward deployment and the shakti member by settled dedication, the reverse of the expected sense sweekruti / swagat sweekruti is the bal The definition places evidencing in projection of what has been received within sweekruti A bal activity defined with projection and evidencing in its own clause santosh / shree santosh is the bal Santosh is “the lack of the sentiment of lacking” and also “readiness for evidencing along with production more than needs” Readiness-for-evidencing language inside a state activity keerti / vichar keerti is the bal Keerti is “the activeness for awakening” Activeness is motion language; both members read as motion shraddha / pujyata shraddha is the bal Shraddha is “movement towards righteousness”; pujyata is “activeness for qualitative development” Both members read as movement; neither reads as a resting state nireekshan / guna nireekshan is the bal Nireekshan is an inspecting activity; guna is “relative motions”, what gets inspected The pair divides as act and object, not as state and motion

passages.heading: 6-where-the-definitions-cut-against-the-column
passages.section: 6. Where the definitions cut against the column
passages.text: Two general points follow. First, several definitions carry both an established clause and a readiness-or-evidencing clause within one activity, on both sides of the partition; the internal grammar of a definition is therefore not a reliable classification criterion. Second, bal and shakti here are not “static” and “dynamic”. A bal activity is an activity, and the sources say so; what distinguishes it is that it is what the faculty has established in itself, which may well be established as an activeness or a movement.

passages.heading: 7-what-the-sources-do-not-settle
passages.section: 7. What the sources do not settle
passages.text: 7. What the sources do not settle

passages.heading: 7-what-the-sources-do-not-settle
passages.section: 7. What the sources do not settle
passages.text: Neither presentation states one general rule for how a shakti member stands to its bal member. The definitions variously concern accepted conditions, readiness for projection, evidence, relationships, responsibilities, acts, objects, sensory qualities, and bodily correlates. The tabulated columns therefore establish assignment without establishing a uniform pair semantics.

passages.heading: 7-what-the-sources-do-not-settle
passages.section: 7. What the sources do not settle
passages.text: This inventory does not sort those relations into a functional taxonomy. A proposed grouping and pair-level schema are kept in the technical companion §8, where their interpretive status is explicit.

passages.heading: 8-variants-and-unresolved-points
passages.text: 8. Variants and unresolved points

passages.heading: 8-variants-and-unresolved-points
passages.text: A second, unpaired list. Before the definitions begin, a shorter run of activity definitions appears without pairing, laid out as a flat glossary (MVD, pp. 323–326). Most of its entries recur in the paired enumeration, sometimes worded differently — medha is “the activity that bears kala” there and “the carrier-bearer activity of memory” in the paired list, and shanti is “behaviour based on resolved thoughts” against “consequence of resolved thoughts”. Two entries in it have no counterpart in the paired enumeration at all: ichchha, desire, as “awareness about one’s wishes and aspirations”, and kalpana, imagination, as “prior form of belief” (MVD, pp. 325–326). Neither appears among the 122. Ichchha is separately the name of chitta’s shakti in the tabulated enumeration, which may account for its absence from the activity list, but nothing consulted accounts for kalpana.

passages.heading: 8-variants-and-unresolved-points
passages.text: Closing names differ between the table and definitions. The AVD table gives chirchira, shvasan–nihshvasan, and swagat–aswagat (pp. 93–94). The detailed MVD definitions instead give charpara, prashvasan–vishvasan, and apanapan–parayapan (p. 348). The inventory rows retain the AVD activity names because that table governs column assignment; their condensed definitions follow MVD. The variants are recorded rather than silently normalised.

passages.heading: 8-variants-and-unresolved-points
passages.text: AVD repeats poshan against temperature and the six tastes. Table 1 prints poshan (nourishing) as the shakti member of rows 24–30, and the English WIP copies the gloss “(nourishing)” onto row 31, whose Hindi is shvasan/nihshvasan, inhalation and exhalation (pp. 93–94). MVD does not name a second activity in rows 24–30. It defines cold, heat, and each taste through poshan/shoshan, then defines nourishing as unit plus conducive unit and depleting as unit minus a conducive unit or plus an unconducive unit (p. 348). The inventory retains the AVD pair assignments and presents the MVD definition view beside them. It does not decide whether repeated poshan denotes seven distinct activities, one recurrent activity, or tabular shorthand. Named poshan also occurs independently at row 21 with mata.

passages.heading: 8-variants-and-unresolved-points
passages.text: Shruti is mistranslated once. The Hindi definition of sauhardta includes smriti aur shruti, memory and shruti (MVD, p. 340). The accompanying English renders the latter “direct recognition,” a term used elsewhere for sakshatkar. The inventory retains shruti and uses its definition as realised articulation from the same activity list (MVD, p. 329).

passages.heading: 8-variants-and-unresolved-points
passages.text: Saujanyata twice. In the detailed definitions the twelfth vritti heading reads “Nyaya (saujanyata), Samvedna”, giving saujanyata parenthetically at nyaya although it is already the shakti member of the tenth pair (MVD, pp. 335–336). The tabulated enumeration has nyaya alone at position twelve.

passages.heading: 8-variants-and-unresolved-points
passages.text: Sound has no pair. The sensory group covers touch, temperature, the six tastes, smell, and visible form. Sound appears inside the definition of priya, among the five organs whose conduciveness it names, but not as a pair of its own (MVD, p. 343). Whether that follows from the enumeration’s principle is open.

passages.heading: 8-variants-and-unresolved-points
passages.text: The counts are stated, not derived. The decomposition into one, two, eight, eighteen, and thirty-two positions is printed with the table but nowhere argued, and the general account of atomic constitution says only that each orbit holds one or more particles (MVD, p. 78). The four orbital terms are the shell capacities 2n2 for n=1 to 4; no consulted passage states that correspondence.

passages.heading: 8-variants-and-unresolved-points
passages.text: What a pair-level specification would need. The enumeration supplies a uniform two-slot form but not uniform fields. Some definitions state a governing criterion or an evidential result and others a single clause, and the tabulated version has five columns with none of the three. A specification giving each pair its content, criterion, relevant relation, and evidential result would therefore have to be constructed rather than read off.
